newsitem.title: USA: U.S. domestic crude grades end dull session steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. domestic crude grades end dull session steady.

text.p: U.S. crudes closed Monday where they began, weakening on an outright basis and holding steady for domestic grade differentials.
Traders generally agreed the session lacked excitement, only moving lower on the losses in refined products futures.
Pressuring heating oil and gasoline values were reports that Sun Co Inc restarted the 85,000 barrel per day (bpd) catalytic cracking unit at its Marcus Hook, Pa. refinery.
In addition, the cat cracker at Venezuela's Amuay refinery was returned to normal operating status late Friday.
December West Texas Intermediate/Cushing closed at $23.80-90 a barrel, down 30 cts from Friday's ending range.

Factors pushing the domestic grade market have been well-established for some weeks: sweets underpinned by weak arbitrage opportunities for Atlantic cargoes and sours depressed by negative fundamentals.
Monday saw the Louisiana sweet market maintain hefty premiums to the WTI/Cushing outright price. Deals were confirmed for Dec Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James between 88-90 cts above WTI/Cushing.
Traders said LLS was talked late in the afternoon at 90-93 cts over the WTI/Cushing, a 2-5 cts gain from Friday.

Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire drifted lower in the mid-afternoon, and ended at a 10 cts discount to the LLS. West Texas Sour/Midland sold at a $1.75 and $1.73 discount to the WTI/Cushing, changing little all session and only a penny off from the Friday finish.

Dec Postings Plus stagnated at $1.88-$1.90, 3-5 cts higher from Friday, fueled by Dec/Jan WTI spreads at 18-22 cts. Cash traders said at some point the level of activity would increase this week, but many refiners were busy much of last week, leaving some doubt on immediate-term needs.
Players were also catching glances at the fact Dec NYMEX futures expire on Wednesday, and some even mentioned that pre-Thanksgiving trading patterns were to blame for the lull.
